record.original_question: For equilibrium measures minimizing the Riesz s-energy with radial external field, for which pairs (s, α) with −2 < s < d and α > max{0,−s} is the support of the equilibrium measure μ_eq full-dimensional, and for which pairs does dimension reduction occur so that supp(μ_eq) has dimension strictly less than d?

evidence.quote: Question 1.2 (Robert Womersley, Edward Saff). When is the support of the equilibrium measure full dimensional and when is the support of dimension less than d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $d\ge 1$ and a parameter $s$ with $-2<s<d$. For a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, define the Riesz $s$-kernel
$$k_s(x,y)=\begin{cases}\|x-y\|^{-s},& s\ne 0,\\ -\log\|x-y\|,& s=0,\end{cases}$$
and, for a radial external field $Q_\alpha(x)=\|x\|^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha>\max\{0,-s\}$, define the weighted energy
$$I_{s,\alpha}(\mu)=\iint k_s(x,y)\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y)+2\int Q_\alpha(x)\,d\mu(x).$$
Under these conditions there exists a unique compactly supported equilibrium probability measure $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}=\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}(s,\alpha,d)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ that minimizes $I_{s,\alpha}$ among all Borel probability measures of finite weighted energy.

Determine, as a function of $(s,\alpha,d)$, the Hausdorff dimension of $\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})$. Specifically, characterize the set of pairs $(s,\alpha)$ with $-2<s<d$ and $\alpha>\max\{0,-s\}$ for which $\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})$ is full-dimensional (i.e.\ has Hausdorff dimension $d$, equivalently has nonempty interior), and the complementary set of pairs for which "dimension reduction" occurs, meaning $\dim_H \operatorname{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})<d$ (for example, the support being contained in a sphere or lower-dimensional subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$).
artifact.category_tag: Riesz equilibrium measures with external fields
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has characterized, for radial external fields that are powers of the Euclidean norm, exactly when the equilibrium measure for the Riesz s-energy concentrates on a sphere (a strongest form of dimension reduction). Complementary results exhibit broad parameter ranges where the support is a full-dimensional ball with explicit (e.g., arcsine-type) density. A complete classification of all pairs (s, α) with −2 < s < d and α > max{0,−s} according to the dimension of supp(μ_eq) does not appear to be settled in full generality, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Riesz Energy with a Radial External Field: When is the Equilibrium Support a Sphere?
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes powers α for which the equilibrium measure for the Riesz s-energy with radial external field |x|^α concentrates on a sphere.
status_evidence.claim: Sphere-supported (dimension-reduced) case characterized for power-type radial fields.

status_evidence.title: Riesz energy problems with external fields and related theory
status_evidence.snippet: General theory of Riesz energy with external fields, including support properties of equilibrium measures.
status_evidence.claim: Provides framework but not a complete (s, α) classification of support dimension.

status_evidence.title: Equilibrium measures for higher dimensional rotationally symmetric Riesz gases
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies classes of confining potentials yielding equilibrium measures supported on the unit ball with explicit density.
status_evidence.claim: Full-dimensional support established in broad parameter ranges.
